2 خبّب , (JK, S, A, K,) inf. n. تَخْبِيبٌ, (JK, TA,) He deceived another; (S, K;) namely, another's young man, or slave: (S:) or deceived much or greatly: (Har p. 591:) and he corrupted another; (JK, A, TA;) namely, another's male or female slave. (TA.) You say, خبّب عَلَيْهِ صَدِيقَهُ, (Aboo-Bekr, TA,) and عَبْدَهُ, and حَلِيلَتَهُ, (A,) He corrupted, and rendered disaffected to him, (Aboo-Bekr, A,) his friend, (Aboo-Bekr,) and his male slave, and his wife. (A.) ＝
-A2- He bound his arm, or hand, with a خِبَّة, i. e. a piece of rag like a fillet. (A, TA.) ＝
-A3- It (one's flesh) wasted so that there appeared streaks upon the skin. (TA.) ＝
-A4- See also R. Q. 1.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
